newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - August 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - August 4.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- SOFTER LINE ON CORPORATE RULES

The Hampel comittee, chaired by ICI chairman Sir Ronnie Hampel, is to announce new guidelines for listed companies to follow and to discuss in their annual reports which will broadly incorperate the principles of the reforms in the Cadbury and Greenbury inquiries but which will aim to meet company complaints of overburdening compliance. The 40-page report is to outline policy issues, governance codes, anti-fraud strategy, the unitary board system and auditing among other issues.
-- EU WANTS LABELS FOR GENETICALLY MODIFIED SOYBEANS

The European Union is drawing up propsed regualtions for November requiring all products containing genetically modified soybeans to be labelled as such after calls from consumer, emvironmental and retail groups urged the move to identify the inclusion of genetically modified organisms in the estimated 60 per cent of prodcts that contain them. Austria, Luxembourg and Italy have already banned imports of genetically modified maize.
-- TESCO CONSIDERS EXPANDING INTO SOUTH-EAST ASIA

It has emerged that UK leading supermarket chain Tesco is considering expanding into south-east Asia after the rapidly growing market has attracted Japanese, US and European chainstore food retailers. Tesco is initially looking to expand into Hong Kong, where it has a purchasing office, and China although there is likely to be serious competition from the Japanese retailer Jusco and French chain Carrefour.
-- PHARMACISTS MAY GET MORE DISPENSING RIGHTS

Health secretary Frank Dobson is considering proposals by large pharmacy chains to allow the pharmacists to diagnose some minor ailments and dispense drugs to patients for treatment in a bid to lighten the workload of family doctors and to trim the 4bn stg NHS drugs bill. The move is opposed by doctors because of public health reasons but the large pharmacies, such as Boots, would welcome the move which would allow them to regian some of their diminishing prescription fees.
-- WARNING ON INTEREST RATES IN EURO-ZONE

French Investment Bank Paribas' chief capital market economist Paul Mortimer-lee has warned that interest rates in the European economic and monetary union could be significantly higher than current national rates based upon an analysis of trends in US and German interest rates. Mr Mortimer-Lee commented that interest rates in the Emu could increase well above the average German rate of 2.5 per cent over the last ten years.
-- GAS ROW ENDS IN RENEWED ROW OVER PIPELINES

Seven weeks since the Monopolies and Mergers Commission set strict efficiency and financial targets for Transco, BG GAS.L has renewed heated debate with Ofgas concerning guidelines from the MMC over Transco's gas shipments that Ofgas believe may be 'understated'. If Ofgas win through it could cost BG 500m stg because of revenue that is significantly above that considered appropriate by the MMC.
-- ITT SEALS $150M HOTEL DEAL

Billionaire Martin Davis' Davis Gaming has bought a 50 per cent stake in The Desert Inn hotel on the Las Vegas strip for $150m cash from the US hotels and leisure group ITT as part of a move by the group to ward off a hostile $6.5bn bid by Hilton Hotels. In a joint venture with Davis Gaming ITT is also to raise $100m from new debt issued.
-- ICI IN $400M SHANGHAI VENTURE

Imperial Chemical Industries has been given approval from the Chinese government for a $400m joint venture to produce 100,000-150,000 tonnes of raw material for use in making polyurethane. The move comes as part of ICI's $500m expansion into polyurethane manufacture in Asia includes a $24m investment into South Korea.
-- TELEWEST CONSIDERS NTL MERGER PROPOSAL

Cable and broadcast services group NTL's chief executive Barclay Knapp has put forward a proposal to the second largest UK cable company Telewest that the two concerns merge to form a group with a combined franchise cover of more than 7m homes, larger than Cable and Wireless Communications' combined franchise cover of 5.4m homes.
-- NETWORK TECHNOLOGY TO RAISE 5M STG IN NEW ISSUE

Print server and networking technology designer and manufacturer Network Technology is to announce plans to move from the Alternative Investment Market to the main market and raise 5m stg in new equity issue despite company shares being at their lowest since November at 164.5p per share compared to the high price in February of 239.5p per share.
